skill.name: sharepoint-audit
skill.description: Guide users through a local SharePoint Online permissions audit using PowerShell, Python, certificate authentication, and generated HTML reports.
skill.summary: Run a local SharePoint Online permissions audit and produce sensitive access reports.
skill.author: Aqualia

security_audit.summary: The audit found no prompt injection or hidden malicious intent in the skill text. The remaining confirmed risks are expected for this skill: it directs the agent to run local PowerShell and Python commands, including module installation, which requires explicit user authorization.

remediation.issue: PowerShell module installation runs local code and may fetch dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Install-Modules.ps1, document the modules installed, and prefer pinned module versions where possible.

remediation.issue: The audit workflow executes a local Python script with tenant and site inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact command before execution and confirm the output directory, tenant ID, site list, and permission scope with the user.

remediation.issue: Generated reports contain sensitive SharePoint permission data.
remediation.suggestion: Remind users to store reports in a protected location and avoid sharing report paths or contents in public channels.

content.value_statement: SharePoint permission audits are difficult to run consistently across sites. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a local audit workflow with certificate authentication and report output.
actual_capabilities: Collects required tenant, app, certificate, domain, and site inputs before running the audit.
Checks that PowerShell 7.4+, Python 3.10+, and PnP.PowerShell are available locally.
Runs the provided PowerShell module installer and Python audit wrapper when authorized.
Supports one SharePoint site or a CSV-defined batch of sites.
Points users to generated HTML reports and warns that reports contain sensitive data.
limitations: Requires local PowerShell, Python, certificate credentials, and appropriate SharePoint permissions.
Does not perform the audit without running local commands on the user machine.
May install PowerShell modules unless the environment is already prepared.
Does not remove or redact sensitive report files after generation.

use_cases.description: Run a guided audit for a sensitive site and generate a local permissions report.

use_cases.title: Audit a site inventory from CSV

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic site audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one SharePoint site.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through auditing one SharePoint Online site. Ask for each required value and show commands before running them.

prompt_templates.title: Check local prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate tools before collecting sensitive inputs.

prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced run with explicit permission scope control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a SharePoint audit command using Sites.Selected Read permission only. Do not use Write permission unless I explicitly approve it.

output_examples.input: Audit this site after I provide tenant ID, client ID, certificate path, and internal domains.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for missing inputs, confirms PFX_PASS is set, shows the module and audit commands, then requests approval before running them.

output_examples.input: The audit finished successfully. What should I open?
output_examples.output: The assistant points to the generated report.html path and warns that the report contains sensitive SharePoint permission data.

output_examples.input: Run this with Sites.Selected Write permission.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains that Read is the default and asks for explicit confirmation before adding the Write permission option.

best_practices: Run the audit from a trusted local environment with PowerShell and Python already reviewed.
Use Sites.Selected Read permission unless Write permission is clearly required and approved.
Store generated reports in a protected folder because they expose permission and access details.
anti_patterns: Do not paste certificate passwords into the chat or command line output.
Do not run module installation commands without reviewing the environment and source first.
Do not share generated report files in public or low-trust channels.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to SharePoint by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides local commands that use your configured certificate authentication and SharePoint permissions.

faq.question: Can it audit more than one site?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports one site URL or a CSV-defined batch of SharePoint sites.

faq.question: Does it require PowerShell?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects PowerShell 7.4+ and PnP.PowerShell to be available locally.

faq.question: Where are audit results stored?
faq.answer: Results are written under a local runs folder, including an HTML report for each audited site.

faq.question: Are the reports sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. The generated reports can contain permission and access details, so store and share them carefully.

faq.question: Can it use Write permission?
faq.answer: The skill defaults to Read permission. It should only use Write permission after explicit user authorization.
